reuse.why: All affected consumers reuse applyWeekendRule, and the new range handler uses the existing recurrence conversion and date utilities.

duplication.why: The off-day policy remains shared, although adjusting occurrences, discarding skipped results and formatting dates repeats across consumers.

placement.why: Recurrence policy stays in shared/schedules.ts, configuration stays in model types, and handler registration follows the existing server structure.

scope.why: The edits cover the requested schedule changes, affected consumers and focused tests without unrelated modifications.

maintainability.why: The central adjustment function is easy to extend, but separate lookahead and range-padding assumptions make occurrence enumeration harder to maintain consistently.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All changed paths delegate weekend and holiday decisions to shared/schedules.ts:applyWeekendRule.

disguised_duplication.where: The repeated occurrence-processing pipeline is straightforward; weekend and holiday policy is shared rather than disguised.

abstraction_drift.where: WeekendRule gains frequency and holidays, and applyWeekendRule gains a daily-frequency skip branch; these represent requested domain variations, and no changed consumer bypasses the helper.
